newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. trade negotiators with China quit.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. trade negotiators with China quit.

text.p: The U.S. government's two top trade negotiators with China plan to leave government, the U.S. trade representative's office said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Jay Ziegler confirmed that Lee Sands, the assistant trade representative for Japan and China, and his deputy, Deborah Lehr, were resigning.

The Washington Post reported in Tuesday's editions that the two were talking to former U.S. trade representative Mickey Kantor about joining his law firm to represent U.S. companies seeking access to China and other Asian markets.
Ziegler said that "any employee in government can resign and seek another job" and that the trade representative's office was working on a "smooth transition."
"It would be a great mistake to read into this a change in policy with regard to WTO negotiations," Ziegler said.
The two were involved in negotiations to allow China to join the World Trade Organisation if China opens its markets sufficiently to foreign trade.
